memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Say to the Israelites: 'Of all the animals that live on land, these are the ones you may eat.'" - Lev 11:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before a single animal is named, notice who is speaking. The LORD said. These food laws did not come from ancient superstition or from someone's opinion about hygiene. They came from God Himself, spoken to Moses and Aaron, and passed on to the people He had rescued out of Egypt.

That matters more than we might think. Israel had just come out of a land where every neighbouring nation had its own gods, its own taboos, its own rules about what was sacred. God's people were not left to guess. Their God spoke clearly, and He spoke about ordinary things — about dinner, about the kitchen, about what goes on the plate.

We sometimes imagine God is interested only in the "spiritual" parts of our lives — our prayers, our Sunday worship, our giving. But here He walks straight into the most daily corner of life. Nothing in your day is too small for God to have an opinion about.

And notice the tone: "these are the ones you may eat." God begins with permission, not prohibition. He is not a stingy Father drawing up a list of what you cannot have. He is a generous One who first says yes.

The same God still speaks to us — now fully and finally through His Son (Heb 1:1-2). Are we listening?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which areas of your daily life do you treat as "too ordinary" for God to care about?
2. When you think of God's commands, do you hear a generous "yes" or only a restrictive "no"?
3. How carefully do you listen when God speaks through His Word?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are a God who speaks, and who cares about even the ordinary corners of my life. Teach me to listen with a willing heart, and help me hear Your voice as the voice of a generous Father. Amen.
